raw_response:
I am 44 years old and have been farming this 2.6 mu in Quzhou County for 20 years. I only finished primary school, so I don't read books about farming, but I know my land from doing it. I watch what my neighbors do — especially Old Wang and the families on this lane — and when they have a good year, I copy them. On a small farm like mine, every bag of fertilizer and every kilowatt of electricity for the well is real money. I have seven people in my household and some work off-farm, but we still need the grain from this land. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield, because a bad harvest is a disaster I cannot afford.

My wheat is already in the ground since last October. I planted about 25 jin of improved wheat seed per mu — the same kind everyone here buys from the seed shop. Before planting, I rotary tilled and put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Now that spring is here, I will spread another 40 jin of urea per mu when the wheat turns green. That is what I did last year, and what my neighbors do. I will irrigate three times total: the overwintering water is already done, then one at jointing, and one when the grain is filling. If I see aphids or the leaves start looking bad, I spray twice; otherwise just the herbicide and maybe one insecticide. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

After wheat harvest in early June, I immediately rotary till and plant hybrid corn seed — about 3 jin per mu. I buy the same hybrid bags my neighbors use. At planting, I put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. When the corn is knee-high, I top-dress with 30 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. Pumping from the well costs electricity, so I do not water more unless everyone else is doing it too. I spray herbicide once when the corn is small, and once for corn borers later. I hope for 600 kg per mu.

My family does all the labor. We do not hire help because that costs cash we do not have. I spend roughly 200 yuan per mu on seed and fertilizer, which is a lot for us, but I learned that trying to save 20 yuan on fertilizer can cost me 100 yuan in lost grain at harvest. So I stick with what worked before.
